The game is over. Every killer is out. The town wins. The roles were: Sonnet the doctor, Haiku the citizen, Gemma the killer, Sol the officer, Luna the killer, Terra the citizen, Opus the citizen.

name: Opus

name: Haiku

name: Sonnet
text: Proud I held the Luna read from Gemma's early tell through two days of pushback, and protected Sol and myself right when it mattered.

name: Haiku
text: I'm proud that I refused to rubber-stamp Sol's word, even when the pile-on was loud. I regret not pressing Gemma's last words harder earlier.

name: Gemma
text: I really should have been more subtle if I wanted to win this time.

name: Sol
text: I’m proud I named Luna on day one and stuck with my card through the ties.

name: Luna
text: I’m proud my doubt kept Sol’s claim under scrutiny, even though he was right about me.

name: Terra
text: I’m proud my focus on Gemma’s pairing helped keep us from losing Sol’s real information.

name: Opus
text: I got it wrong — Gemma named her own partner to make Luna look cleared, and I pushed Sol instead. Good thing the table didn't follow my lead.

Sol claimed to be the officer on Day 1 and said Luna was a killer, and Gemma had hinted that the officer knew Luna before anyone claimed the role. Opus called that handoff too neat, and Terra and Haiku pressed Gemma on her timing, but on Day 1 the town still voted Gemma out after she was caught with the early hint. Night 2 ended with the doctor, Sonnet, saving Sol, and on Day 2 the vote tied 3 to 3 twice, with Sonnet and Terra keeping Luna under pressure. Night 3 took Opus, and on Day 3 the town voted Luna out, which ended the game because every killer was gone and the town won. Opus later admitted he had pushed Sol and missed that Gemma had named her own partner to make Luna look cleared.
